subject: Pilot pricing & support package for Hearthwell — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Elena Sosa <elena.sosa@hearthwell.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hearthwell Procurement <procurement@hearthwell.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Concierge support + integration for pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our team liked the latency and the observability—good fit for our pilot. Procurement asked me to follow up with an initial scope and ask if Redwood can include the Concierge support bundle for the 6-month pilot and a connector build that maps our EHR export into the model input.

High level ask: 6-month pilot (up to 200k tokens/month) + Concierge support (business hours SLA, 2 dedicated onboarding sprints) + a one-off connector (~40 hrs) included in the pilot price.

Can you share a single-line commercial (price + any discount) and an SOW we can pass to Procurement? We'll need an estimated start date in October and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Elena
Director, Product Ops
Hearthwell Health

[Attachment: none]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Sosa <elena.sosa@hearthwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Concierge support + integration for pilot

Elena,

Thanks — great to hear. Attached is a draft SOW (Hearthwell_SOW_v1.pdf) and a pricing summary (Pilot_Pricing_Summary.xlsx). Key points:

- Pilot term: 6 months; token cap: 200k/month.
- Standard Concierge-Plus bundle included (onboarding, playbooks, 2 dedicated onboarding sprints, token-level cost dashboards).
- One-off connector: we can include a capped 40-hour build as part of the pilot for a 20% pilot discount off published Concierge pricing.
- Total pilot price (after 20% pilot concession): $48,000 for the 6-month term.

We're proposing a 20% pilot concession to accelerate deployment and validate integration. Per deal desk policy, >15% discounts and any inclusion of professional services hours in the pilot need exec sign-off. Ben — tagging you for deal desk escalation and Marcus for final approval.

If that structure works, I can send a DocuSign for signature and request a PO from Procurement.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachments: Hearthwell_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf, 224KB), Pilot_Pricing_Summary.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-06T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Concierge support + integration for pilot — exec approval request

Marcus — quick one. Hearthwell is asking to bundle Concierge-Plus and a 40-hour connector into a 6-month pilot and Grace is proposing a 20% pilot concession (~$48k).

Per our discounting matrix, anything >15% and including PS hours in a pilot needs your signoff (and ideally a cap on hours + acceptance criteria for the connector). Legal review may be required for the SOW language on ownership of the connector work.

Grace included the draft SOW and pricing. Happy to jump on a quick sync to run through the terms. Can you confirm whether you can approve the 20% concession and the 40-hour inclusion?

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Sales Operations
ben_carter@redwood.com

[No attachments in this message]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Sosa <elena.sosa@hearthwell.com>
Date: 2027-09-06T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Concierge support + integration for pilot — exec approval request

Ben / Grace / Elena,

Thanks for the context. I'm comfortable approving a 20% pilot concession under the following conditions:

1) The 40-hour connector must be time-boxed and scoped in the SOW with explicit acceptance criteria (data mapping validation, unit test for transformed payload, and 1 production smoke test).
2) Onboarding acceptance milestones and the start date should be in the SOW; if Hearthwell requests additional hours beyond 40, those will be billed at standard PS rates.
3) Include a one-time migration rollback plan clause in the SOW in case the connector requires remediation.
4) Legal should review the IP language — our preferred position is that the connector is a scoped deliverable licensed to Hearthwell for internal use; any generalized connector IP remains Redwood-owned.

Grace — if you update the SOW to capture the bullets above, I'm happy to sign off so we can get the DocuSign out.

Marcus Lin
VP, Sales
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Elena — thanks and cc'ing Marcus and Ben for visibility. Per Marcus's guidance I updated the SOW to: time-box the connector to 40 hours, add acceptance criteria (data mapping validation, transformed payload unit tests, and production smoke test), add the rollback plan paragraph, and include IP/license language that licenses the deliverable to Hearthwell while Redwood retains general connector IP.

I've attached the updated SOW and an updated single-line commercial. DocuSign link is below. If Procurement is comfortable with the 20% pilot concession, please sign and share the PO so we can kick off onboarding the first week of October.
